title: PLC #4 — Tractor Engine (J1939)
description: Engine telemetry decoded from the JD 5055E CAN bus. PROPOSED, not deployed. Every panel reads plc4_engine / plc4_dtc_* from migration 067. A gap in a series means the engine did not broadcast that PGN — not that the value was zero.

panels.title: Engine speed
panels.description: SPN 190, PGN 61444. Resolution 0.125 rpm. Absent while the key is off.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS time, rpm FROM plc4_engine WHERE $__timeFilter(recv_ts) AND rpm IS NOT NULL ORDER BY recv_ts

panels.title: Coolant and oil temperature
panels.description: SPN 110 (coolant, PGN 65262 byte 1) and SPN 175 (oil, bytes 3-4).

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS time, coolant_c AS "coolant", oil_temp_c AS "oil" FROM plc4_engine WHERE $__timeFilter(recv_ts) AND (coolant_c IS NOT NULL OR oil_temp_c IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY recv_ts

panels.title: Oil pressure
panels.description: SPN 100, PGN 65263 byte 4. Wire resolution is 4 kPa (0.58 psi) — the trace is genuinely stepped, and that is the sensor, not the plot.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS time, oil_kpa FROM plc4_engine WHERE $__timeFilter(recv_ts) AND oil_kpa IS NOT NULL ORDER BY recv_ts

panels.title: Battery and keyswitch potential
panels.description: SPN 168 (battery, PGN 65271 bytes 5-6) and SPN 158 (keyswitch, bytes 7-8). Below 12.2 V running means the alternator is not keeping up.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS time, batt_v AS "battery", keysw_v AS "keyswitch" FROM plc4_engine WHERE $__timeFilter(recv_ts) AND (batt_v IS NOT NULL OR keysw_v IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY recv_ts

panels.title: Engine hours
panels.description: SPN 247, PGN 65253. MAY READ 'No data' FOREVER: this PGN is on-request for many engines and the board does not transmit requests. An empty panel here is an open question, not a fault.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS time, hours FROM plc4_engine WHERE hours IS NOT NULL ORDER BY recv_ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: CAN liveness (frames/min)
panels.description: Rate of change of the board's lifetime frame counter. Zero with the key on means the transceiver, the wiring or the bus has dropped — the engine panels would simply go blank and tell you nothing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS time, (frames - LAG(frames) OVER (ORDER BY recv_ts))::double precision / NULLIF(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (recv_ts - LAG(recv_ts) OVER (ORDER BY recv_ts))) / 60.0, 0) AS "frames/min" FROM plc4_engine WHERE $__timeFilter(recv_ts) ORDER BY recv_ts

panels.title: Lamps
panels.description: DM1 lamp states. 0 off, 1 on, 3 not available. A steady 3 means the ECU does not implement that lamp.

targets.rawSql: SELECT mil AS "MIL", rsl AS "Red stop", awl AS "Amber", pl AS "Protect" FROM plc4_dtc_snapshot ORDER BY recv_ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Active DTCs
panels.description: The most recent DM1 snapshot. An empty table with a recent timestamp means the ECU reported no active faults; an empty table with no timestamp means no DM1 has ever arrived. The age column is how you tell.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recv_ts AS "reported", age_s AS "age (s)", n AS "count", spn AS "SPN", fmi AS "FMI", oc AS "occurrences" FROM v_plc4_dtc_active ORDER BY spn NULLS FIRST
